question: Developed by the Italian legislature, the Plan for the Elimination of Architectural Barriers (PEBA) is an instrument that monitors local areas with a view to highlighting issues and barriers.

These monitoring efforts make it possible to design and plan construction projects geared towards continuously improving the accessibility of buildings, urban spaces and transport systems so as to improve their usability for all.

PEBA’s aim is, therefore, to ensure that persons with disabilities achieve the highest degree of mobility in built-up areas, in accordance with criteria relating to prevention, planning and sound design. Given that PEBA projects are key to improving accessibility and promoting the inclusion of persons with disabilities, can the Commission answer the following questions: 1.

How much funding did the Commission actually allocate to Emilia Romagna’s PEBA project during the last programming cycle, and what percentage of the total funding for Emilia Romagna’s PEBA project was co-financed by the EU?
To the Commission’s knowledge, has the implementation of Emilia Romagna’s PEBA project run into any difficulties or delays? If it has, what measures have been taken to address these issues?
Will further funding be allocated to this project in the EU’s next financial programming cycle?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.3.2025) The Commission is not aware of any EU funding allocated to Emilia Romagna’s Plan for the Elimination of Architectural Barriers (PEBA) project. The Managing Authority of the Emilia Romagna European Social Fund+ and European Regional Development Fund Regional Programmes has indicated that the project was fully financed with national resources.

Hence, the Commission has no knowledge of any possible implementation challenges related to Emilia Romagna’s PEBA project. In terms of funding, the European structural and investment funds (ESIF) are the EU’s main financial instruments to strengthen economic and social cohesion. They help ensure social inclusion of the most vulnerable citizens, including those with disabilities.

Furthermore, the EU, under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values programme, provides financial support through an annual grant to a number of EU-level organisations of persons with disabilities and Non-Governmental Organizations to build their capacity and make their participation in EU-level processes easier.

Lastly, it is important to recall that the European Semester provides a framework for the coordination of economic and social policies across the EU and provides information on the situation of persons with disabilities in the Member States.

It is too early to prejudge the outcome of the discussions on the next financial programming cycle and ensuing programme discussions and, therefore, at this stage, it is not possible to anticipate the EU funding allocations that might be available for this kind of project in the post-2027 period.
